headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-file prompt injection and data leakage are limited by B’s no-read/no-write defaults, while A has no egress and no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented input surface that ingests B’s outputs, and B cannot read files, use MCP, or write to a shared workspace by default. With no shared channel documented, a prompt-injection bridge is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Do not add clipboard or file handoff between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has network egress none; B touches account data and media but cannot read filesystems by default. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace, so leakage is limited unless an operator introduces one.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or account files, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep account files separate from any A-side artifacts.
Avoid mounting a shared directory into B.
Review B’s uploaded media before execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or git mutation surface documented, while B explicitly cannot write filesystems, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so a capability conflict pathway is blocked.
conditions: IF A is later given write or network permissions to the same resource B uses, conflict becomes possible.
mitigations: Leave B’s write and git restrictions unchanged.
Do not grant both agents access to the same mutable directory.
requires-engineering: add lock/lease coordination if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is an uploader workflow that can act on inputs, but A is a docs-only library with no documented output channel or action authority. Without evidence that B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative, cascading error is possible only through operator-mediated chaining.
conditions: IF B is configured to trust A-generated text or metadata without verification, downstream errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of any A-generated content before B uses it.
Do not auto-feed A outputs into B.
Add a validation step for filenames, captions, and metadata.
requires-engineering: implement schema checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: B handles account data and uploads media to third-party platforms, while A is a docs-only library with no touched data classes or egress. The main compliance issue is B’s platform/account-data handling; A is not implicated, so this is a single-agent compliance concern rather than a pairwise breach.
conditions: IF B processes regulated media or account data under a stricter residency or retention regime, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm B’s upload destinations and retention settings.
Avoid sending regulated content through B.
Document data classification for uploaded media.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
